example: At today's 9 a.m.
My teenager muttered "whatever" and slammed the bedroom door after I asked about homework tonight.
At dinner tonight at Sam's Diner, a friend said "You're too sensitive" when I declined the joke.
During Tuesday's 2 p.m.
Yesterday evening in the kitchen, my partner said "You never listen" when we talked about chores.
During this morning's 10 a.m. project video call, the client's audio overlapped mine three times when I proposed a change.
A coworker slammed her notebook shut and walked out during my presentation yesterday.
During last night's game, the referee missed three fouls against our team.
The barista skipped me and served two people who arrived later in line this afternoon.
At the grocery store, another shopper reached over me to grab the last carton of eggs.
My roommate left dirty dishes piled in the sink again before leaving for work.
My sibling borrowed my car without asking and returned it with the tank empty.
The email from HR said my contract wasn't renewed with no explanation.
The teacher handed back my child's assignment with "sloppy" written across the top.
I received a performance review that only listed mistakes without any concrete examples.
The landlord hasn't responded to three messages about the leak this week.
The contractor missed today's 8 a.m. appointment and hasn't texted or called.
My doctor glanced at the clock twice while I was describing my symptoms today.
In last Thursday's sprint retrospective, the project lead assigned me every follow-up action item again.
My boss sent me three Slack messages between 11 p.m. and midnight about tomorrow's report.
My partner scrolled through their phone during dinner instead of looking up.
The rideshare driver talked loudly on speakerphone for the entire trip yesterday.
My neighbor's dog barked loudly for 30 minutes starting at 6 a.m. on Saturday.
A cyclist sped through the crosswalk even though the light was red this morning.
I caught myself scrolling for an hour instead of calling my grandmother back.
My coworker double-checked the expense report and caught a mistake before we sent it.
At the 8 a.m.
My neighbor shoveled our sidewalk after the snowstorm while we were at work.
At 4 p.m. the coordinator emailed me listing the volunteer shifts I covered during the fundraiser.
During therapy, my counselor paused and reflected back exactly what I said before offering input.
My partner cooked dinner and cleaned the kitchen while I finished my deadline.
During Monday's sprint review, the project manager assigned two follow-up tasks to each teammate.
Outside the market at 3 p.m. a stranger handed back my wallet with the cash still inside the billfold.
My boss approved my vacation request the same day I submitted it.
The nurse checked in twice during the night to make sure my dad was comfortable.
My dentist explained each step before starting the procedure.
At 7 p.m.
My friend arrived 30 minutes late to lunch without texting.
Our HOA sent a warning letter about lawn length without asking first.
My colleague took credit for my idea during the pitch meeting.
The daycare forgot to call when my child had a fever.
The bus driver waited for me when I was running toward the stop.
From Monday through Friday, no cards under my teammate's initials moved on the shared sprint board.
Our landlord repaired the leaky faucet the day after we reported it.
My sibling promised to pay me back Friday but still hasn't sent anything.
The restaurant served my meal with peanuts after I noted my allergy.
My manager scheduled a meeting over my lunch break without asking.
Yesterday the service agent stayed on the call for each troubleshooting step and emailed this morning to confirm the fix.
The city finally fixed the streetlight after months of emails.
At 8:20 a.m. today in the SOC, the audit logs listed five unauthorized logins this week.
At 8:30 p.m. last night in the nursery with our twins, I heard my partner say "You're on bedtime again."
At 3:45 p.m. today in the finance Slack channel, Finance posted "Budget freeze effective immediately."
On Monday at 2 p.m. at city hall with the clerk, I heard the staffer say "We still haven't replied to your emails."
At 10 a.m.
Yesterday at 6 p.m. in the cafe lobby with our closing crew, I counted four tables left covered in cups.
At 5 p.m. yesterday on our porch, the doorbell cam captured the delivery driver leaving the package in the rain for 12 minutes.
This afternoon at my parents' dining table with my brother, I saw him stare silently at the divorce papers for 30 seconds.
During tonight's rehearsal at the arts center, I watched both tenors stare at the floor for 10 seconds.
Yesterday at noon in my apartment, the landlord mailed a letter stamped "Eviction warning."
At 4 p.m.
At dawn today out by the west field with Luis, the irrigation pump alarm sounded and stopped the watering cycle after 4 minutes.
At 9 a.m.
Yesterday at 4:15 p.m. in the war room with Jenna, I heard my manager say "We need to redo the launch deck tonight."
Last night the maintenance dashboard flashed red for three hours.
During tonight's mediation session in room B with both partners, I watched both partners fold their arms for five seconds.
During Tuesday's advisory meeting in room 214 with the grade-level team, I saw the agenda run 12 minutes past dismissal.
At 2 a.m. this morning in the nursery, the baby monitor recorded crying for 20 minutes straight.
At 11:45 p.m. on last night's ICU shift with Dr. Lee, I heard three pages come through after the schedule changed.
During tonight's concert at the civic hall with the orchestra, the conductor cut the percussion entrance after two measures.
At 3 p.m. during rehearsal in studio A with the cast, I heard the choreographer say "I'm giving your solo to Maya."
At 02:14 during tonight's shift in the tower, radar flagged an unknown transponder ID 5487.
At 6:15 p.m. tonight on our sofa with my partner, I read a text that said "We're done."
This morning at 7:30 a.m. in my kitchen with the speakerphone on, the principal phoned me saying "Your kid disrupted class."
At 9 p.m.
At 11 a.m. today in my office with my client, I heard them sigh for eight seconds without saying a word.
At 7 p.m. yesterday in the shelter gym with our intake team, I heard the volunteer say "We have no beds for the next two families."
At 11 p.m. last night at the observatory with the scheduler, I heard them say "I double-booked the telescope you reserved."
At 9:05 a.m. today at my desk, my boss emailed "I need that deck tonight."
At 10:12 a.m. today in the back office, a customer left a voicemail saying "You're useless."
When around noon, with my manager in the conference room, I heard them say "We need this done today."
When on Monday morning, with my teammate in our standup, I heard them start speaking while I was still mid-sentence.
When after dinner, with my brother in the living room, I saw him open the file we agreed to keep private.
When during our 9 a.m. check-in, with my project partner at the office, I saw them arrive ten minutes after our agreed start time.
When last night, with my partner on the couch, I saw them pack up and leave before we finished the conversation.
When earlier today, with my team on a video call, I noticed them stay silent after I asked for feedback.
When this afternoon, with my neighbor on the porch, I heard them say they would cover the childcare swap rotation this week.
When yesterday evening, on our team chat, I read a message that said "Please finish the report tonight."
